intended_object: The coordinatewise map ι → R → ι → S, x ↦ (i ↦ f(x i)), packaged as a semilinear map along f.op for the right-module structures. It exists only to be fed into `fromSemilinear` to build `rightFreeTo`, the forward half of the equivalence identifying the scalar extension of ι → R along f with ι → S. Inferred from the docstring and from how the file uses it.
explanation: The definition is a construction step used only once: `rightFreeTo := fromSemilinear f (rightFreeToSemilinear f ι)`. The file's mathematical content is `rightFreeLinearEquiv`, the isomorphism (ι → R) ⊗_R S ≅ ι → S of right S-modules; this map is just the semilinear input needed to define its forward direction. The body is correct. Additivity follows from f.map_add, and compatibility with the right action, f(x i · r) = f(x i) · f(r), follows from f.map_mul. The section variables [Fintype ι] and [DecidableEq ι] are included automatically but are not used by the body, and only semirings would be needed. Since this is an internal helper rather than a standard notion, that unnecessary restriction is not judged as a narrowness defect. No dedicated Mathlib declaration packages this coordinatewise map as an f.op-semilinear map.
